questions.q: Which letter is 7th to the left of P in the English alphabet?
questions.solution:
P is the 16th letter. Moving 7 places left: $16 - 7 = 9$, the 9th letter is I.
**Answer: I**
questions.shortcut: Count from A = 1; subtract positions to move left.

questions.q: Choose the address that is the same as the one given below. 12/5A, Rajaji Nagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka-560010
questions.solution:
Compare each option word by word with the original. Option 3 reproduces the address exactly — house number, locality, city, state and PIN 560010 — while the others change the PIN digits or drop the house number.
**Answer: 12/5A, Rajaji Nagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka-560010**
questions.shortcut: Check the PIN and punctuation first; distractors alter digits.

questions.q: Three seminars were conducted in Guwahati, Itanagar, and Shillong on 2nd, 3rd, and 4th April. Shillong was scheduled after Guwahati. Itanagar was not on 4th April. When was Shillong's seminar?
questions.solution:
Shillong must be after Guwahati, and Itanagar cannot take 4 April. If Guwahati were on 3rd, Shillong would need 4th and Itanagar 2nd — valid; if Guwahati is on 2nd, Itanagar on 3rd forces Shillong to 4th. In every valid case Shillong falls on 4 April.
**Answer: 4th April**
questions.shortcut: Fix Itanagar ≠ 4th, then test the two orders.

questions.q: Seminar in Siliguri was 3 days after Darjeeling, and Kalimpong hosted its seminar 1 day before Siliguri. If Darjeeling was on 2 March, when was Kalimpong's seminar?
questions.solution:
Darjeeling on 2 March puts Siliguri on 5 March (3 days after), and Kalimpong, one day before Siliguri, is on 4 March.
**Answer: 4th March**
questions.shortcut: Chain the offsets: 2 → 5 → 4.

questions.q: Consider the following statement and choose the option that follows. Statement: The bank has introduced QR-code-based transactions at all branches. Inferences: I. Customers are expected to use digital methods more. II. Traditional banking counters will be phased out.
questions.solution:
Inference I is a reasonable expectation from introducing QR-code transactions. Inference II (phasing out counters) is an extreme prediction the statement never supports.
**Answer: Only I follows**
questions.shortcut: Reject inferences with 'will be phased out' style absolutes.

questions.solution:
The rule is $a \times b + 4$: $6 \times 2 + 4 = 16$ and $7 \times 3 + 4 = 25$, so $8 \times 4 + 4 = 36$.
**Answer: 36**
questions.shortcut: Test a×b+4 against both clues first.

questions.q: What should come in place of the question mark '?' in the following number series? 14, 26, 50, 98, 194, ?
questions.solution:
Each term is $\times 2 - 2$: $14 \to 26 \to 50 \to 98 \to 194 \to 386$.
**Answer: 386**
questions.shortcut: Differences double: 12, 24, 48, 96, 192.

questions.q: What will come in the place of question mark (?) in the following number series? 2, 3, -1, 8, -8, ?
questions.solution:
Differences alternate in sign and grow as perfect squares: $+1, -4, +9, -16$, so the next difference is $+25$: $-8 + 25 = 17$.
**Answer: 17**
questions.shortcut: Slopes 1², 2², 3², 4², 5² alternating.

questions.q: If digits of 642 are reversed and added to the original number, what is the result?
questions.solution:
Reversing 642 gives 246; $642 + 246 = 888$.
**Answer: 888**
questions.shortcut: Straight reversal and add.

questions.q: Which is the odd one out?
questions.solution:
Table, fan and bed are furniture/man-made household objects; the kidney is a body organ, so it does not belong.
**Answer: Kidney**
questions.shortcut: Three artefacts vs one body part.

questions.q: Which code has a digit-letter sequence that doesn't follow a repeated unit?
questions.solution:
Options 1, 2 and 4 repeat an identical 4-character unit twice (1A2B•, 3C4D•, 7G8H•). In 5E6F7E6F the second half starts with 7, breaking the repeat.
**Answer: 5E6F7E6F**
questions.shortcut: Test whether the string equals its own first half repeated.

questions.q:
Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark [?] in it.

14  12  7   15
21  29  15  18
245 287 154  ?
questions.solution:
In each column, (top + middle) × 7 = bottom: $(14+21) \times 7 = 245$, $(12+29) \times 7 = 287$, $(7+15) \times 7 = 154$. Hence $(15+18) \times 7 = 231$.
**Answer: 231**
questions.shortcut: Look for a column-wise multiply rule; the ×7 is constant.

questions.q: You're a forest officer and a local festival causes pollution in a sensitive zone. What is your best step?
options: Coordinate with local leaders for eco-friendly celebrations
questions.solution:
The constructive step is to engage stakeholders and steer the festival towards eco-friendly practices; banning, ignoring or abandoning the zone are extreme or negligent responses.
**Answer: Coordinate with local leaders for eco-friendly celebrations**
questions.shortcut: In ethics items, pick the balanced, cooperative action.

questions.q: Identify the number which does NOT belong to the group:
questions.solution:
11, 13 and 17 are prime; 15 = 3 × 5 is composite, so it does not belong.
**Answer: 15**
questions.shortcut: Scan for the only composite.

questions.q: Find the option that does not fit the series pattern; 7, 12, 19, 28, 39, 51, 67, 84
questions.solution:
Correct gaps grow as 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17: the series should read 7, 12, 19, 28, 39, 52, 67, 84. The printed 51 breaks the pattern (39 + 13 = 52), so 51 is incorrect.
**Answer: 51**
questions.shortcut: Differences should be consecutive odd numbers.

questions.q: Directions: Study the following information carefully and answer the questions based on it. Comprehension: Seven boxes are kept one above another to make up a stack. The topmost box is numbered as 1, while the b numbered as 7. Each box contains different fruits, including Apples, Oranges, Cherries, Bananas, Melons, Kiwis, and Mangoes. Each box contains a different number of fruit: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, and 70. There are 20 oranges. The box of Bananas is two boxes above the box of Melon. There are 70 Melons. There are 20 and 60 fruits in the topmost and bottommost boxes respectively. The box of Apples is just above the box of bananas. The box of Kiwi is just above the box of Mango. There are 30 Cherries in the box. The box containing 50 fruits is just above the box containing 10 fruits. There are ___ Apples.
questions.solution:
Topmost box has 20 fruits and there are 20 oranges ⇒ box 1 = Oranges; box 7 = 60. Melons (70) sit two below Bananas, and Apples sit just above Bananas, forcing Melon at 5, Bananas at 3, Apples at 2. The '50 just above 10' rule then fixes box 2 = 50, box 3 = 10, leaving Kiwis 40 at 6 and Mangoes 60 at 7, with Cherries 30 at 4. So there are 50 Apples.
**Answer: 50**
questions.shortcut: Place the fixed counts (20 top, 60 bottom, 70, 30) first, then link Bananas–Melon–Apples.

questions.q: Directions: These questions are based on the following information. In a family there are eight members, P, Q, R, S, T, U, V, and W. V is the sister of the mother of U. W is the father of Q who is the brother of U. R is married to V. T is the father-in-law of W. S is the daughter of R. How is P related to S?
questions.solution:
W is father of Q and U, so W's wife is their mother; T being W's father-in-law makes P (the only remaining member) that wife, i.e. mother of U. V, sister of U's mother P, and S being R and V's daughter, means P is S's mother's sister — her maternal aunt.
**Answer: Maternal Aunt**
questions.shortcut: Anchor on 'T is father-in-law of W' to place P as the mother.

questions.q: Direction: These questions are based on the following information. There is a family of 7 members: Puja, Payal, Paras, Preet, Palak, Pia and Parth. In that family, there are 3 generations having 2 married couples among them. Preet is brother in law of Paras. Puja is daughter in law of Pia. Pia and Parth is married couple who has only 1 son. Palak is sister of Payal. Payal is daughter of Paras. Parth is father of Paras. How many male members are there in a family?
questions.solution:
Pia–Parth are one couple; their only son is Paras, so Puja (daughter-in-law of Pia) is Paras's wife. Payal and Palak are Paras's daughters. Preet, brother-in-law of Paras, is Puja's brother. Males: Parth, Paras and Preet — three men.
**Answer: 3**
questions.shortcut: Two fixed couples + 'only 1 son' pins the generations.

questions.q: Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows. Statement: All books are papers. Some papers are journals. Conclusions: I. Some journals are books. II. Some papers are books.
questions.solution:
'All books are papers' converts to 'some papers are books', so II follows. From 'some papers are journals' nothing forces any journal to be a book, so I does not follow.
**Answer: Only II follows**
questions.shortcut: Universal statements convert to particular; 'some' never converts to 'all'.

questions.q: Read the following statement carefully and identify the conclusion that follows. Statement: Some cars are electric. All electric vehicles are eco-friendly. Some eco-friendly things are expensive. Conclusions I. Some cars may be eco-friendly II. Some expensive things are not cars.
questions.solution:
Cars that are electric must be eco-friendly, so 'some cars may be eco-friendly' is a valid possibility. Conclusion II would need expensive things that are not cars, which the statements never guarantee.
**Answer: Only I follows**
questions.shortcut: 'May be' conclusions follow whenever the possibility is not contradicted.

questions.q: Complete the series. A1, C2, E3, G4, ?
questions.solution:
Letters advance by 2 (A, C, E, G, I) and numbers by 1 (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), so the next term is I5.
**Answer: I5**
questions.shortcut: Two independent tracks: letter +2, digit +1.

questions.q: What is the next number in the series? 1, 4, 16, ____
questions.solution:
Each term is ×4: $1, 4, 16, 64$.
**Answer: 64**
questions.shortcut: Geometric with ratio 4.

questions.q: Which of the following is different from the rest?
questions.solution:
11, 13 and 17 are prime; 21 = 3 × 7 is not, so it is the odd one out.
**Answer: 21**
questions.shortcut: Only composite in the group.

questions.q: What comes next? 5, 10, 8, 16, 14, ?
questions.solution:
Pattern alternates ×2 and −2: $5 \times 2 = 10$, $10 - 2 = 8$, $8 \times 2 = 16$, $16 - 2 = 14$, so next $14 \times 2 = 28$.
**Answer: 28**
questions.shortcut: Alternate operations ×2, −2.

questions.q: Identify the group that does NOT match the consecutive pattern. PQ, QR, RS, ST, SV
questions.solution:
PQ, QR, RS, ST are pairs of consecutive letters; SV skips U, so it breaks the pattern.
**Answer: SV**
questions.shortcut: Check letter gaps: all should be +1.

questions.q: What comes next? AA, BC, CE,?
questions.solution:
First letters move +1 (A, B, C, D) and second letters move +2 (A, C, E, G), giving DG.
**Answer: DG**
questions.shortcut: Two tracks: +1 and +2.

questions.q: If STORM is coded as RSNQL, how is SHINE coded?
questions.solution:
Each letter of STORM is shifted one step back: S→R, T→S, O→N, R→Q, M→L, so SHINE → RGHMD.
**Answer: RGHMD**
questions.shortcut: Uniform −1 shift.

questions.q: If LAVEN is written as NEVAL, how is DAISY written?
questions.solution:
LAVEN reversed is NEVAL, so DAISY reversed is YSIAD.
**Answer: YSIAD**
questions.shortcut: Pure reversal coding.

questions.q: Complete the series. 91, 86, __ 76, 71
questions.solution:
The series falls by 5 each step: 91, 86, 81, 76, 71.
**Answer: 81**
questions.shortcut: Constant −5.

questions.q:
What word is formed by (0,4), (4,3), (2,1), (3,4) using the grid below (row, column)?

    0  1  2  3  4
0   J  B  D  C  L
1   F  I  A  J  H
2   D  A  K  L  E
3   B  K  G  I  A
4   K  C  E  L  L
questions.solution:
Reading (row, column): (0,4) = L, (4,3) = L, (2,1) = A, (3,4) = A — the word LLAA.
**Answer: LLAA**
questions.shortcut: Index the grid as (row, col) and read off.

questions.q: The series given below contains a sequence of numbers. Accordingly identify the INCORRECT number. 40, 40, 37, 31, 21, 10
questions.solution:
Differences should fall as 0, 3, 6, 9, 12 (multiples of 3): 40, 40, 37, 31, 22, 10. The printed 21 (which would need a difference of 10) is the incorrect number.
**Answer: 21**
questions.shortcut: Gap check: 31 − 21 = 10 breaks the −3, −6, −9, −12 run.

questions.q: Complete the analogy. F : I :: L : ?
questions.solution:
F (6) → I (9) is +3; L (12) + 3 = 15, which is O.
**Answer: O**
questions.shortcut: Alphabet positions and a fixed +3 jump.

questions.q: Complete the analogy. ZYX : WVU :: TSR : ?
questions.solution:
ZYX, WVU, TSR are blocks of three letters descending; after TSR (T, S, R) come Q, P, O, so the answer is QPO.
**Answer: QPO**
questions.shortcut: Each block is the next 3 letters down the alphabet.

questions.q: Find the missing term in the series: A, C, F, J,? A, C, F, J, ?
questions.solution:
Gaps increase: A +2 = C, C +3 = F, F +4 = J, J +5 = O.
**Answer: O**
questions.shortcut: Skipping 1, 2, 3, then 4 letters.

questions.q: Select the option that does NOT belong to the same category as the others: Amazon, Nile, Mississippi, Sahara
questions.solution:
Amazon, Nile and Mississippi are rivers; the Sahara is a desert, so it does not belong.
**Answer: Sahara**
questions.shortcut: Three water bodies vs one desert.

questions.q: In five even-numbered houses, 10-18: K lives at the top; J is one house above H; L is the lowest; M is between H and K. Who is at 14? Who is at 14?
questions.solution:
Houses 10–18: L is lowest (10), K at top (18). J one above H and M between H and K forces H = 12, J = 14, M = 16 (only then does M lie between H = 12 and K = 18). So 14 holds J.
**Answer: J**
questions.shortcut: Fix L and K first; test the two orders for H, J, M.

questions.q: Statement: "To promote reading, the library will start weekend storytelling sessions for children." Which conclusion follows?
options: The library wants to attract young readers
Storytelling is the only reading activity planned
questions.solution:
Storytelling sessions for children show the library aims to draw young readers. The other options overstate ('only children visit'), contradict ('adults dislike weekends') or exaggerate ('the only reading activity').
**Answer: The library wants to attract young readers**
questions.shortcut: Pick the moderate, directly supported conclusion.

questions.q: In a heated group discussion, what should an emotionally intelligent person do?
questions.solution:
Emotional intelligence calls for self-control and empathy: calmly hearing both sides before responding. Taking sides, shouting or storming off all escalate the conflict.
**Answer: Calmly listen to both sides**
questions.shortcut: In EQ questions, the calm, balanced option wins.

questions.q: You notice your manager is unusually silent in a crucial meeting after a recent personal loss. The team expects decisions. What is the best action?
options: Take the initiative for key discussions and offer support afterwards
Remain silent until the manager speaks
Ask intrusive questions about their loss
questions.solution:
The professional response is to step up and keep decisions moving while offering the manager private support afterwards — it serves the team without intruding on personal grief. Silence, prying or criticism are all unhelpful.
**Answer: Take the initiative for key discussions and offer support afterwards**
questions.shortcut: Balance task needs with empathy, no intrusion.

questions.q: Arrange as per dictionary order and select the word that is second in order: CLINIC, CLING, CLINK, CLINT
questions.solution:
After CLIN-, compare the 5th letter: G < I < K < T, so the order is CLING, CLINIC, CLINK, CLINT. The second word is CLINIC.
**Answer: CLINIC**
questions.shortcut: Common prefix — rank by the first differing letter.

questions.q: If 'P is husband of Q' and 'R is son of Q', how is R related to P?
questions.solution:
P is Q's husband and R is Q's son, so R is the son of P as well.
**Answer: Son**
questions.shortcut: Same mother, married parents → son.

questions.q: Find the odd one out in the given semantic series based on the pattern identified. Iron, Platinum, Zinc, Lead
questions.solution:
Iron, zinc and lead are common base metals; platinum is a rare precious metal, so it is the odd one out.
**Answer: Platinum**
questions.shortcut: Three base metals vs one noble metal.

questions.q: Complete the analogy. Clock : Time :: Thermometer : ?
questions.solution:
A clock measures time just as a thermometer measures temperature. (Mercury is merely the medium.)
**Answer: Temperature**
questions.shortcut: Instrument : quantity it measures.

questions.q: Complete the analogy. Evaporate : Vapour :: Condense : ?
questions.solution:
Evaporation produces vapour as condensation produces liquid — the analogy pairs each process with its product state.
**Answer: Liquid**
questions.shortcut: Process : resulting state of matter.
